rationale: Exact 2019 Carpene chapter abstract lists cranberry Vaccinium macrocarpon juice and ex-vivo enzyme activity; proposes possible mood relevance but gives no human mood measurements. Publisher body inaccessible; preserve original outcome scope pending and do not equate an enzyme assay with clinical depression.

Review abstract names cranberry among menopausal plants; publisher original body does not name Vaccinium macrocarpon or identify a cranberry exposure or depressive-symptom trial. General symptom claims concern other plants; cranberry taxon and supporting citation remain unresolved.

Wicks and Mahady chapter first online 2014-12-18; publisher abstract lists cranberry among common herbs and depression among general indications without linking them or reporting outcome. Original body pages 373–399 not accessed; cranberry-specific section and citations remain open.

Identical 2026 Irani chapter source summary describes berries and cranberry in antioxidation, inflammation and cancer prevention; no depression result in this summary. Publisher exact chapter blocked, so its complete content remains pending.

2017 collection of 2016 special issue reprints, full 156-page publisher PDF; extracted text has no depression match; cranberry review addresses cancer and cells, other human cranberry studies cover metabolic outcomes. The neurological article studies berry extracts in cells, not human depression or Parkinson disease.

Identical 2026 Razzaghi chapter source summary discusses oxidative stress and cranberry among several berries; no depression result in the summary. Publisher exact chapter blocked, so complete content remains pending.

Bratman and Girman 2003 Mosby handbook has separate cranberry and depression entries in book contents; its actual relevant entries unavailable. Another similar-named Skidmore-Roth book is a different source and cannot resolve this record.

Norman and Butrum introduction 3729S–3730S in 2003 nutrition/cancer supplement; PubMed PMID14608106 describes entire 3729S–3873S proceedings and is not an article-specific abstract. Publisher PDF access denied; no claim about its specific text or other child presentations.
Avery 2013 evidence-resource listing pp E3–E11, PubMed assigns breastfeeding as indexed topic, but no abstract/full resource entries retrieved; cannot infer cranberry or depression absence.
